name: Madiao
description: Madiao is a historical Chinese money-card game with trick-taking and gambling structure, traditionally played with a dedicated 40-card money-suited deck.

overview.description: Madiao is a historical Chinese money-card game with trick-taking and gambling structure, traditionally played with a dedicated 40-card money-suited deck.

history.origins: Madiao is one of the classic Chinese money-card games and is historically important in the development of East Asian card and tile traditions.
timeline: Ming era: Madiao is documented as an established Chinese money-card game.
Later centuries: money-card traditions influence later families including khanhoo and eventually Mahjong.
history.cultural: Madiao belongs to the historical Chinese money-card tradition that later shaped several draw-and-discard and tile-based game families.
history.evolution: Rules and deck composition varied by region and era, but Madiao remains one of the best-known early money-card trick-taking families.

setup.players: Four players in traditional banker-versus-others style structures.
setup.dealing: Cards are dealt to the four players according to the local Madiao procedure before trick play begins.
setup.equipment: Madiao cards and stake or score tracking according to table custom.

rules.objective: Win the valuable cards and scoring outcomes defined by the table’s Madiao rules through controlled trick play.
rules.gameplay: Players use the dedicated money-card pack in a trick-taking structure with suit-following, high-card resolution, and gambling-style settlement conventions determined by the chosen ruleset.
keyRules: Madiao uses a dedicated Chinese money-card deck, not a French or tarot pack.
The game is trick-taking and gambling-oriented rather than meld-based.
Suit order, priority cards, and settlement depend on the historical ruleset being used.
Control of high-value cards and tempo determines the result.

strategy.basic: Protect the strongest money cards and avoid giving away control of the scoring cards too early.
strategy.intermediate: Track which suit groups have already been exhausted so you can time high-card captures more precisely.
strategy.advanced: Use trick timing and information from exposed cards to force opponents into disadvantageous leads and protect settlement-critical cards.
tips: Count exposed high cards carefully; information matters quickly in small dedicated packs.
Do not waste control cards on low-value tricks unless it prevents a larger scoring swing later.

scoring.description: Scoring follows the local Madiao ruleset, with valuable cards, trick outcomes, and gambling-style settlement determining the result.
scoring.winCondition: The side or player who captures the required value under the chosen Madiao settlement rules wins the hand or session.
